title: Add a seeded ontology file with a structure test and decision record
summary: Answer yes to decision 5: add docs/ontology.toml, a small vocabulary of defined terms with sources and relations, seeded with the seven misreads Sri listed, plus a Rust test that validates it and a decision entry. Audience: agents that read it, checks that parse it, and Sri judging it.

defaults_applied.how: The structure test is Rust; no scripts.
New test, cargo test, clippy and fmt --check required.
Terms defined for an outside reader with cited sources.
Every term carries a verifiable source.
No secrets or email address in new files.
Test enforces sources, relations and uniqueness.
Test must fail on bad input, not just check the file exists.
One file, one test, one decision entry.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The file is machine-readable TOML (docs/ontology.toml) so checks can parse it; the repo already uses docs/decision-links.toml.
The new decision gets the next free id after D108 (D109); the producer checks decisions.md for the current highest id and for any link-table requirement in docs/decision-links.toml.
The test lives in an existing crate's tests dir (athena-cli/tests) and uses crates already in the workspace (toml/serde) rather than adding a new dependency.
Term sources are repo paths or decision ids that exist; BRIEF.md addenda are cited by path plus addendum heading and the test checks the file and heading text exist.

Seven terms: planning, job, Athena, Hermes, product versus system, landed, Sri. Each records the misread, definition, source and relations; relation targets must be defined terms, so supporting terms (e.g. Olympus, firstmate, Hermes Agent, study) are added only if needed as relation targets and each carries a misread or is avoided.
Sri's pronoun rule (refer by name or as they) is a term definition; the file itself uses they/Sri only.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/ontology.toml exists with the seven seeded terms (planning, job, Athena, Hermes, product versus system, landed, Sri). Each has a definition, the misread that caused it, a source naming a path or decision id that exists in the repo (planning: BRIEF.md addendum 2026-10-16 'Speed, planning first' and D105; job and Athena: addendum 2026-10-17: Olympus; Hermes: Part 2 S1; product versus system: the Olympus relay note), and relations whose targets are all defined terms.

The file states that a term is added only when it causes a misread, and says how a check reads it (the parse path and fields). The landed term says merged on main through a verified pull request. The Sri term says to use the name or 'they', never he or she, and cites job 20261017-173504-91ys.

docs/decisions.md has a new entry keeping the ontology, citing the Olympus 2026-10-17 decision sheet (decision 5), listing alternatives (no ontology; per-study glossaries only), and stating that studies keep their own concept model so firstmate, Hermes Agent and Athena are compared in the same terms. Any decision-link or index file the repo requires for new decisions is updated.

Run `cargo test`: a new test parses docs/ontology.toml and passes, and the test is written to fail on a missing or non-existent source, a dangling relation target, or a duplicate term (negative cases covered by unit tests on in-memory input). `cargo clippy` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
No secrets or personal data, including the user's email address, appear in any new or changed file.

out_of_scope: Changing any study's own concept model or files under studies/
Wiring the ontology into agent contexts or token budgets beyond the file and its test
Adding terms not caused by a misread
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows
